solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thin tree chopped up, a number being bad

indicators.note: a tree chopped up is cut into pieces, so the letters of the two words are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A spindly tree is felled, and some figure is said to be unlucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped up' rearranges THIN TREE. Thirteen is the number traditionally thought unlucky, hence 'a number being bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the figure superstition holds to be unlucky, so it is a number considered bad.

clue.text: Spare key, yours some time ago?

parts.note: spare in the sense of lean or skinny means thin
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone offers a spare key and asks whether it was once yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like 'extra' attached to the key; here it means lean.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the archaic possessive form for 'your' or 'yours' used when addressing one person, as in old poetry and the Bible.

clue.text: Coroner's investigation of death during hunt

parts.note: during something is being in it
a hunt or search is a quest

explanation.surface: A coroner looks into a death that happened while a hunt was on.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner holds a formal judicial inquiry into the cause of a sudden or unexplained death.

clue.text: Transporter of seeds was first in the conurbation here

parts.note: pointing to something here, one says this

indicators.note: in places the words for leading inside the word for the urban area

parts.note: a conurbation is a large built-up area, loosely a town
to be first in a race is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone claims a place here was the first conurbation to do something, with seeds oddly involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was first' means led, as a front-runner does in a race; 'the' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fluffy down on thistle heads carries their seeds away on the wind.

clue.text: Newspaperman given some credit, organisationally

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A journalist is given some credit for being well organised.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'given', which is only a link word joining definition and wordplay; the definition is 'Newspaperman' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper's content, deciding what is printed, is a newspaperman.

clue.text: I turn back behind unknown Hindu ascetic

indicators.note: behind puts the reversed piece after the letter for the unknown

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x and z

indicators.note: back says the words for I and turn are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to have a turn is to have a go

explanation.surface: Someone turns back behind a mysterious holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses I GO to give OGI, which sits 'behind' Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu holy man who practises yoga and renounces comforts is a classic ascetic.

clue.text: Rather large robes employed, but not all

indicators.note: only part of the words robes employed is used, a run of letters spanning both

explanation.surface: Somewhat roomy robes are put to use, though not every one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very overweight is a polite-ish understatement as 'rather large'.

clue.text: Perfect day in Scilly I, going about topless

indicators.note: in places the letter for day inside the reversed letters
going about means turning round, so the trimmed letters are read in reverse
topless means the top, or first, letter of the island name is removed

explanation.surface: A perfect day on the Isles of Scilly, wandering about without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' cuts SCILLYI to CILLYI, 'going about' reverses it to IYLLIC, and D goes in. The Isles of Scilly are islands off Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyllic scene is blissfully happy and unspoilt, as near flawless as can be.

clue.text: One vinyl is quiet, playing in a curious manner

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: playing suggests a record spinning and the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A single vinyl record is quiet while it plays, in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' here means nosy, not odd, despite the strange image of a quiet record.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking questions out of eagerness to know is acting in a nosy, prying way.

clue.text: Taking it easy after middle of winter is potentially appealing

indicators.note: after places the word for relaxing behind the central letters
the middle of a word is all of it except its first and last letters

parts.note: taking it easy is resting

explanation.surface: Relaxing in midwinter sounds like an attractive idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' takes INTE from wINTEr, all but its end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that holds the attention and arouses curiosity has the makings of being appealing.

clue.text: Throw out English judge before European court

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge, as in law reports

explanation.surface: An English judge is expelled before a case reaches the European court.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone forcibly from a place is to throw them out.

clue.text: Round tamale that's mixed up milled grain

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the word tamale is mixed up, its letters jumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A round Mexican tamale gets mixed up with some ground cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: A tamale is a Mexican dish of maize dough steamed in a husk.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats ground into meal give a coarse flour used for porridge and baking.

clue.text: Boy wizard too much wrapped up in short hair style

indicators.note: wrapped up in puts the excess piece inside the shortened hairdo
short means the last letter of the word for the hair style is dropped

parts.note: a perm is a hair style of set waves or curls
OTT means over the top, too much

explanation.surface: A young wizard is hidden under an overdone short haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy wizard' points to a surname, not a type of magician; OTT is the British shorthand for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry of that surname is the famous schoolboy wizard of J. K. Rowling's novels.

clue.text: Pull off penning religious books, whatever comes

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals are penned, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to pull off feathers or petals is to pluck
OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: Someone pulls off a feat while writing about scripture, ready for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing but means shutting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking your chances means accepting whatever happens to be available, as at a shared meal.

clue.text: Caper left one in short dress

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the shortened dress
short means the last letter of the word for the dress is dropped

parts.note: a frock is a dress
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A capering girl leaves one item in a short dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful skip or prank, and a romp of that sort is a lively bit of fun.

clue.text: Student left with something quite profitable

parts.note: an earner is something that brings in money, as in 'a nice little earner'

explanation.surface: A student departs with a nice little moneymaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being taught or studying a skill, such as a novice driver, is a student.

clue.text: Some eye queen with time for golf?

indicators.note: with joins the letter for time to the word, entering as a replacement
for says the letter for time stands in place of the letter for golf

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, as in the royal cipher
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A queen keeps an eye on the clock instead of playing golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eyeball is part of an eye, so 'some eye'.

clue.text: Young swimmer initially drowning, passed out in story

indicators.note: in places those first letters inside the word for the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A story tells of someone drowning and passing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies to all three words, giving D, P, O, set inside TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog's larva is a juvenile creature that swims in ponds before growing legs.

clue.text: Vessel contains a gold coin from the past

indicators.note: contains means the word for the vessel holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a duct is a tube or vessel in the body carrying fluid

explanation.surface: A ship's hold contains an old gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a body tube.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a gold coin once used across much of Europe, notably in Venice.

clue.text: Small stringed instrument needing tuning?

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A little stringed instrument needs tuning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on music: a note pitched too high is out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A note slightly above its proper pitch is out of tune and so needs adjusting.

clue.text: Support from chirpy Londoners

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Cheerful Londoners offer their support.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel tower holding up power lines is a structural support.

clue.text: Unlimited oil and unction flowing

indicators.note: flowing suggests liquid moving about, so the letters of the three words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil and anointing ointment pour out without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: Unction is an anointing with oil, as in religious rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolute and without conditions or restrictions is unlimited.

clue.text: Christopher E Bird

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher, as with Kit Marlowe

explanation.surface: Christopher E. Bird reads like a person's full name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a name with a middle initial; Bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey of the hawk family with a forked tail goes by this name.

clue.text: Hot ire over sycophantic follower

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ire is anger
over in the sense of on top of is on

explanation.surface: Heated rage is directed at a fawning toady.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who clings to a person of influence to gain favour is a fawning hanger-about.
